description: Python RAG pipeline — ingest local docs, chunk, embed via sentence-transformers, store in Chroma, retrieve top-k, answer via a local LLM (Ollama by default). Production-shape retrieval-augmented generation with langchain-core primitives. For knowledge-base chatbots, internal search, and doc Q&A products that keep their own corpus.

commands: python -m src.pipeline ask 'what is paged attention?'

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick this when the product owns its document corpus and needs grounded, citation-bearing answers. Ships end-to-end: ingest → chunk → embed → Chroma → retrieve → LLM. For raw LLM serving without retrieval, use vllm-server / tgi-server / ollama-server; for agentic tool-using loops, use agent-service-py.
firstSteps: pip install -e . to install the package and all langchain/chroma deps
cp .env.example .env; verify LLM_BASE_URL points at a running Ollama (`ollama serve`) or OpenAI-compatible server
python -m src.pipeline index — builds the Chroma collection
gotchas: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is 384-dim. Mixing embeddings from different models in the same Chroma collection will silently return garbage — always nuke VECTOR_DB_DIR when you change EMBEDDING_MODEL.
Chroma persists SQLite + parquet to VECTOR_DB_DIR. Commit it to git only for tiny demo corpora; for real docs, rebuild on deploy.
Chunk size tradeoff: too small (<200 chars) loses context; too large (>1500) dilutes retrieval. Default is 800 chars with 120 overlap — tune per corpus.
If LLM_BASE_URL is Ollama you must `ollama pull {{llmModel}}` before the first query — first run otherwise 404s on the /api/chat call.
pypdf is imported lazily. PDF ingest requires `pip install pypdf`; the default install only handles .md and .txt.
Embedding the whole corpus is O(docs × tokens × embedding-forward-pass). For >10k docs use an ONNX/GPU sentence-transformers backend or batch via an embeddings API.

placeholders.description: docs/ (replace sample.md with the real corpus)
src/pipeline.py (chunk size, retrieval k, prompt template)
